why_static: Computed offline from the native rasters and served as a static asset. The deployed backend has no access to these files (/data/ and *.tif are gitignored, and the paths in mission_service.py are Windows absolutes), so on Render it degrades to a seeded DEMO generator and returns fabricated values with HTTP 200. The headline verdict must not depend on that path.
supersedes: the headline verdict previously taken from GET /api/mission/{crater} -- which returned data_mode DEMO with mean_cpr 0.525, max_cpr 2.292, P(ice) 0.96, screening PASS, 5/5 evidence ticks and 17,580,000 m3 of ice, none of it measured

grid.note: Native resolution. The backend request path resamples to 100 x 100 (process_real_dem target_shape) and takes every statistic over the padded frame; nothing here is resampled and nothing is averaged across the void.

elevation.product: LOLA LDEM_80S_20M V2.0, 20 m/px native, low-passed and resampled to 25 m grid
elevation.resample: DOWNSAMPLE — the output grid is COARSER than the 20 m measurement, so content between 40 m and 50 m wavelength cannot be represented and is low-passed away before sampling rather than allowed to alias
elevation.resolution_caveat: Native post spacing is 20 m. Any slope, roughness or hazard quantity derived from this raster is a 20 m quantity resampled onto a 25 m grid, not a 25 m measurement. Label derived tables with the post spacing they were computed at.
elevation.elevation_datum: heights above a sphere of radius 1,737,400.0 m (1737.4 km), the label's own A_AXIS_RADIUS. Not a geoid, not local mean terrain, and not a height above the LRO orbit.

dem_identity.explanation: Holds measured LOLA topography bit-for-bit, verified against lola/ldem_frame_25m.tif at tolerance 0.0 on every run by assert_dem_is_lola(). Called dem_native_synthetic.tif until Phase 6; renamed because a filename asserting 'synthetic' over a real measurement is a provenance defect, not a cosmetic one.

boulder.reason: No boulder detector and no optical product exist in this build; data/pradan/ohrc/ is empty. Boulder risk is UNMEASURED, not zero. The weight is dropped and the blend renormalised over slope and roughness, so hazard is a two-term hazard and says so.

hazard_model.note: Slope and roughness both come from measured LOLA topography, so the hazard blend is measured too -- but it is a two-term blend at 20 m posts, not the three-term one config.py describes. 20 m-POST QUANTITY. The gradient is taken on the 25 m grid, but LOLA measured the surface at 20 m posts and the upsample added no relief below that. Read this as a 20 m slope, not a 25 m one. Elevation is LOLA LDEM_80S_20M V2.0, 20 m/px native, low-passed and resampled to 25 m grid. Despite its filename, native/dem_native.tif holds that measured LOLA topography bit-for-bit (verified every run: max|diff| 0.0 m against lola/ldem_frame_25m.tif); the name is retained only so existing consumers keep working.

illumination_model.method: horizon computation: for each azimuth, horizon(az) = max over r of atan((h(p + r*u) - h(p)) / r), lit when the solar elevation exceeds it
illumination_model.algorithm: O(n) skyline scan per row (Dozier/Frew), verified against an O(n^2) brute force to 1.7e-06 on white, smooth, spiky and monotone profiles
illumination_model.computed_over: the FULL LOLA polar array, not the frame -- at the pole the horizon is set by rim crests tens of kilometres outside this 165 x 56 km frame, and a horizon computed only inside it would invent sunlight that real terrain blocks
illumination_model.subsolar_band_integration: closed form between the band endpoints; sin(el) is evaluated exactly at dec = -1.54 and +1.54 deg and the horizon crossing is interpolated between them. Verified against a 20,001-sample brute force to 0.00059 of the band (0.06 %) over 25 (cos H, horizon) combinations x 5,000 latitudes.
illumination_model.solar_elevation_formula: sin(el) = sin(lat) sin(dec) + cos(lat) cos(dec) cos(H)
illumination_model.why_not_a_flat_cap: 1.54 deg is the Moon's obliquity, which bounds the SUBSOLAR LATITUDE, not the solar elevation seen from a site. Max elevation at latitude phi is 1.54 + (90 - |phi|): 1.54 deg at the pole but 6.71 deg at this frame's outer edge (-84.833408). A flat 1.54 deg cap inflated this array's PSR from 26,900 to 65,398 km2 and would not have looked wrong.
illumination_model.sun_state_model: az uniform over 360 deg; subsolar latitude uniform over +/-1.54 deg (the Moon's obliquity). The solar ELEVATION is then computed PER PIXEL from its own latitude by sin(el) = sin(lat) sin(dec) + cos(lat) cos(dec) cos(H) -- it is not sampled directly, because a fixed el range is correct only at the pole and under-illuminates this frame by up to 4.4x. illumination_fraction is the fraction of SAMPLED SUN STATES in which the point is lit: a geometric visibility fraction, NOT a time-weighted illumination and not a duty cycle. psr_mask (never lit) is independent of that weighting question.
illumination_model.psr_definition: illumination_fraction == 0, i.e. lit in no sampled sun state

doubly_shadowed.definition: never directly lit AND, in every one of the swept azimuths, the crest forming this point's horizon is itself never directly lit
doubly_shadowed.approximation: Tests the BOUNDING CREST per azimuth, not every cell visible below it, and models no multiple scattering or thermal re-radiation. A floor called doubly shadowed here could still receive some scattered light from lit terrain lying below a dark crest.
doubly_shadowed.not_the_old_proxy: The discarded version was the brightness proxy's shadow intersected with the lowest elevation quintile of the DEM. An elevation percentile is not a shadowing event.

illumination_model.resolution_caveat: Computed from 80 m LOLA posts decimated 3x to 240 m. Any resampling onto a finer grid adds no shadow detail; read this as a 240 m shadow mask however it is displayed.
illumination_model.replaces: clip(hillshade(sun_altitude=1.5 deg, azimuth=315 deg) * elev_norm ** 1.3, 0, 1) < 0.05 -- an invented brightness proxy with no horizon term, which darkened 77.18 % of the frame

amplitude.meaning: DFSAR amplitude returned here. Every MEASURED statistic uses this mask only.

footprint.meaning: ISRO sri_ma > 0: where the beam was pointed. 56.11 % of it returned literal zero.

thresholds.note: Not retuned. Lowering CPR_THRESHOLD until this scene passes would manufacture a detection out of an incomplete product.

provenance_legend.MEASURED: An observation, or a direct geometric consequence of one: calibrated Chandrayaan-2 DFSAR radar, or LOLA topography.
provenance_legend.MODELLED: A model output with no ground truth in this project to check it against: the illumination proxy, and the Random Forest P(ice).
provenance_legend.DERIVED: An assumption model applied on top of a measured or modelled quantity.
provenance_legend.UNAVAILABLE: Cannot be computed honestly in this build. Render an em dash and the reason.

criteria_uninformative.label: DOP depressed (volume scattering)
criteria_uninformative.reason: Satisfied by 92.7 % of measured pixels because the amplitude proxy collapses when the two receive channels are balanced, which is the ordinary case over regolith. It is not evidence of volume scattering, and it would read the same over bare rock.

verdict.criteria_note: 0 of 5 evaluable criteria passed INFORMATIVELY. 1 further passed for a reason unrelated to ice and is shown as such rather than as a tick: Satisfied by 92.7 % of measured pixels because the amplitude proxy collapses when the two receive channels are balanced, which is the ordinary case over regolith. It is not evidence of volume scattering, and it would read the same over bare rock. The other 1 are WITHHELD, not failed: two shadow terms awaiting the Phase 2 horizon computation, and thermal stability, for which no product and no model exist here. A withheld criterion is not evidence against ice.
verdict.label: No radar ice signature in this swath
verdict.sublabel: 0.00 km² of the 1,461 km² measured swath passed CPR > 1.00 and DOP < 0.13

headline.note: Area whose measured radar passes both polarimetric criteria, inside the amplitude mask. No shadow term is in this mask: the illumination proxy was removed from it, and the horizon computation that would replace it is Phase 2.

verdict.null_result_caveat: This is a NULL RESULT on an incomplete measurement, not evidence against ice. Peak CPR in the swath is 0.0534 against a 1.00 threshold — the product cannot reach it, because this build derives CPR from amplitude alone. The Stokes S3 phase term from the complex sli products is required before this scene can be screened at all.

thermal_stability_k.note: INFERRED FROM ILLUMINATION, NOT FROM MEASURED TEMPERATURE. No thermal product is on disk and no thermal model runs here. A surface lit in none of the sampled sun states has no direct solar input, and the water-ice stability limit over geological time is about 110 K; the 2,043.2 km² of PSR in this frame is therefore inferred to sit below it. The 110 K figure is an assumed threshold from the literature, not something measured here. If a Diviner product is ever ingested this becomes MEASURED and nothing else changes.

p_ice_max.reason: WITHDRAWN, not missing. The Random Forest behind this figure was fitted to np.random.uniform labels with a fixed seed, and its ice class was defined as CPR 1.05-2.5 -- a range this amplitude-only product cannot reach at all, since the swath's peak CPR is 0.0534. Every probability it produced was an extrapolation from fabricated examples, and one of its six features was the illumination proxy. It is unwired, not retrained: better synthetic labels are still synthetic. Step 4 now reports the criteria screen, which is measured.

landing_site.reason: Not computed in THIS file, and not substituted here. The sites are computed by Phase 3 -- search_landing_sites.py, the argmax of a six-criterion search over all 14,943,444 native 25 m pixels with 5 km non-maximum suppression -- and served from docs/landing_sites.json, which is what the map draws and what the Landing Sites stage reports. What this file will not do is restate them: two copies of one answer is how the site markers and the search came to disagree about where the same five points were. The value that WAS here until Phase 3 was the best of five hardcoded grid offsets (18,50 / 82,75 / 78,25 / 50,15 / 48,85), asserted and then scored, with lat/lon from a flat 30.37 km per degree constant wrong by about 57x in longitude at this latitude. It is recorded here because it shipped.

cpr_dop_identity.consequence: No pixel with DOP < 0.13 can exhibit CPR > 0.0042611, whatever the terrain and whatever the instrument. The configured CPR_THRESHOLD of 1 is 235x above that ceiling, so this screen is LOGICALLY EMPTY, not merely unsatisfied. A candidate area of exactly 0.0 is the only arithmetically possible answer, and a non-zero value here would be a bug rather than a detection.
cpr_dop_identity.what_fixes_it: The true Stokes forms are built from DIFFERENT combinations of the four Stokes parameters -- CPR = (S0 - S3)/(S0 + S3) and DOP = sqrt(S1^2 + S2^2 + S3^2)/S0 -- so they are genuinely independent and their conjunction selects a real population. The amplitude proxy's defect is not that it is small: it collapses two independent physical observables onto one degree of freedom. Phase 5b.

evidence.label: CPR above CBOE threshold
evidence.note: Peak CPR across all 2,337,086 measured pixels is 0.0534, 19x below the 1.0 threshold. This build's CPR is sigma_sc/sigma_oc from amplitude alone; true hybrid-polarity CPR needs the Stokes S3 phase term from the complex sli products, which are not ingested yet.

evidence.label: DOP depressed (volume scattering)
evidence.uninformative_reason: Satisfied by 92.7 % of measured pixels because the amplitude proxy collapses when the two receive channels are balanced, which is the ordinary case over regolith. It is not evidence of volume scattering, and it would read the same over bare rock.
evidence.note: 92.7 % of measured pixels sit below 0.13. PASSES FOR A REASON THAT IS NOT ABOUT ICE: this build's DOP is |tanh(x/2)| with x = ln(LH/LV), so it measures channel imbalance, and balanced channels are what regolith normally gives. Depolarised returns are consistent with volume scattering, but on their own they do not discriminate ice from fine dry regolith -- and this proxy does not measure depolarisation in the first place. See METHODS 7.9.2.

evidence.label: Local incidence in the Bragg domain
evidence.uninformative_reason: The product's incidence raster is not an incidence angle: 80.53 % of its values over the valid mask are below the label's own look angle of 19.9979 deg, which is geometrically impossible on a convex body; its median pixel-to-pixel step is 35x the geometric ramp; and it correlates with DEM slope at -0.0006, so it is not a local incidence either. The field cannot be re-derived from the label, which carries no ephemeris, to the accuracy a 20 deg threshold needs. The criterion is withheld rather than estimated.
evidence.note: Adopted from Putrevu et al. 2023 section 4, and WITHHELD. Withheld is different from failed: this says the criterion could not be evaluated on this product, not that nothing passed it.

evidence.label: Overlap with a shadowed cold trap
evidence.note: TESTABLE NOW. The frame holds 2,043.2 km² of permanently shadowed terrain (21.88 % of it), from a horizon computation rather than a brightness proxy. This row fails because the CANDIDATE set is empty — no pixel clears CPR — not because there is nowhere cold to look. The two are different findings and this build can now tell them apart. Horizon computation over the full 2533x2533 LOLA polar array at 240 m (80 m posts decimated 3x), swept over 360 azimuths. The solar elevation is computed PER PIXEL from its own latitude and the subsolar band is integrated in closed form; it reaches 15.64 deg at this frame's outer edge, not a flat 1.54 deg. az uniform over 360 deg; subsolar latitude uniform over +/-1.54 deg (the Moon's obliquity). The solar ELEVATION is then computed PER PIXEL from its own latitude by sin(el) = sin(lat) sin(dec) + cos(lat) cos(dec) cos(H) -- it is not sampled directly, because a fixed el range is correct only at the pole and under-illuminates this frame by up to 4.4x. illumination_fraction is the fraction of SAMPLED SUN STATES in which the point is lit: a geometric visibility fraction, NOT a time-weighted illumination and not a duty cycle. psr_mask (never lit) is independent of that weighting question. READ THIS AS A 240 m QUANTITY however it is displayed: resampling it onto the 25 m grid adds no shadow detail.

evidence.label: Overlap with a doubly-shadowed core
evidence.measured_label: candidate area inside a doubly-shadowed core
evidence.note: 0.48 km² of this frame is never directly lit AND has no sunlit crest bounding its view in any swept azimuth. Tests the BOUNDING CREST per azimuth, not every cell visible below it, and models no multiple scattering or thermal re-radiation. A floor called doubly shadowed here could still receive some scattered light from lit terrain lying below a dark crest. Fails here because the candidate set is empty, not because no such terrain exists.

evidence.label: Thermal stability expected
evidence.note: INFERRED FROM ILLUMINATION, NOT FROM MEASURED TEMPERATURE. A surface lit in none of the sampled sun states receives no direct solar input, and the water-ice stability limit over geological time is about 110 K. No Diviner or other thermal product is on disk; the 110 K figure is an assumed threshold from the literature. This row follows the PSR-overlap row exactly — it is an inference from the same mask, not an independent temperature test, and it is marked DERIVED for that reason.

notes: Every number in this file is reproducible by re-running the generator; nothing is hand-entered.
MEASURED statistics are taken over the amplitude mask at native 25 m/px. The API's equivalents average across the never-observed void and are therefore lower by construction.

The DEM is measured LOLA topography (LOLA LDEM_80S_20M V2.0, 20 m/px native, low-passed and resampled to 25 m grid), verified bit-identical to lola/ldem_frame_25m.tif on every run, so elevation, slope, roughness and hazard are MEASURED. They are 20 m-post quantities on a 25 m grid and are labelled with the 20 m spacing they were computed at, not the grid they are carried on.
Illumination, PSR and the doubly-shadowed mask are the one remaining invented model here: a brightness proxy with no horizon term. They stay MODELLED, and PSR area stays UNAVAILABLE.
Boulder risk is NO DATA, not zero. The hazard blend drops its weight and renormalises over slope and roughness, so hazard is a two-term hazard in [0, 1] and hazard_model says so.

P(ice) is WITHDRAWN, not downgraded. Its Random Forest was fitted to np.random.uniform labels whose ice class (CPR 1.05-2.5) lies entirely outside this product's achievable range, so every prediction was an extrapolation from fabricated examples. Step 4 reports the measured criteria screen instead.

The candidate mask is (CPR > threshold) AND (DOP < threshold) AND amplitude mask. The illumination proxy's shadow was removed from it: darkening 77 % of the frame discriminates nothing, and its presence made a MEASURED-marked area partly modelled.

The sensitivity sweeps are computed by re-thresholding the native arrays, not by scaling a baseline. Every area column is a pixel count; every volume column is that area times a stated depth and pore fraction.
The screening threshold was NOT retuned to make this scene pass.
A FAIL here is a null result on an incomplete product, not evidence against ice.
